label: Root links from Kevin Richardson, Grounding is Necessary and Contingent
summary: PDF pp. 14–18 (printed pp.465–469), section 6.1: Richardson's what-grounding makes necessity part of the real-definition explanation. This warrants testing the case premise on that reading. The admitted complete-ground relations must realize such real definitions before that defense transfers. PDF pp. 19–21 (printed pp.470–472), section 6.2: Richardson proposes contrastive why-explanation as a different ground relation. On it, difference-making can hold without necessitation. This is a positive rival if the case records track why-explanation. Its applicability to those records and their modal scope remains open.
